highWaterAgeHours.notes: TCEQ identifies high water age (dead-end mains, storage tanks, overlapping pressure planes) as where nitrification usually appears first, without a numeric hour cutoff. 48 h is a versioned operational planning horizon, not a regulatory limit.

elevatedWaterTemperatureC.notes: Nitrifier growth is reported as favorable between about 15 and 30 °C; activity slows below about 10 °C. Health Canada notes typical reported episodes at 20–25 °C. V1 uses the start of the favorable growth range.

lowMonochloramineResidualMgL.notes: Health Canada, citing U.S. EPA (1999), Norton and LeChevallier (1997), and Skadsen and Cohen (2006): preferably greater than 1.5 mg/L monochloramine at all distribution monitoring points as a nitrification-prevention practice. Not a universal safe/unsafe residual.

freeAmmoniaPresentMgNL.notes: TCEQ: free ammonia leaving the plant should be less than 0.1 mg/L, preferably less than 0.05 mg/L. V1 treats ≥ 0.05 mg-N/L as free ammonia present at a level those sources treat as worth controlling.

unusedDrivers.DEPOSIT_OR_SEDIMENT_FACTOR: Not emitted in V1. TCEQ notes sediment can harbor nitrifiers, but VeinGuard has no sediment/deposit field on the V1 network state.

references.citation: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality. Controlling Nitrification in Public Water Systems with Chloramines.

Health Canada (2018). Chloramines in Drinking Water — Guideline Technical Document. Nitrification-prevention residual practice 2 mg/L leaving the plant and preferably >1.5 mg/L in distribution; typical reported episodes 20–25 °C.

Kirmeyer / distribution-system reviews compiled in Kulkarni et al. and related nitrification reviews: favorable nitrifier growth about 15–30 °C; slows below about 10 °C. Used as literature support for the 15 °C driver, not as a probability model.
U.S. EPA (1999). Alternative Disinfectants and Oxidants Guidance Manual. Cited by Health Canada for the ≥1.5 mg/L distribution residual practice.
